intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1A) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (NR3C2; 600983) on chromosome 4q31.23.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1A) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene NR3C2.
checks.evidence_quote: These findings demonstrate that heterozygous MLR mutations cause PHA1
checks.explanation: The abstract says heterozygous mineralocorticoid receptor (MLR = NR3C2) mutations cause PHA1, and these mutations were found in the dominant kindreds.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 gene is located on chromosome 4q31.23.
checks.evidence_quote: we have screened the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (MLR) for variants
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. Under the rules, a gene's chromosomal location counts as standard nomenclature, so the claim is accepted.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I is a form of mineralocorticoid resistance limited to the kidney (Hanukoglu, 1991). In the dominant kindred reported by Hanukoglu (1991), the disorder presented in infancy with renal salt wasting and hyperkalemia, and hyperaldosteronism was documented. Plasma renin activity was raised at first but fell gradually to near-normal values. Geller et al. (1998) described autosomal dominant PHA1 as a milder disease that remits with age.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I is a form of mineralocorticoid resistance limited to the kidney.
checks.evidence_quote: we conclude that type I PHA includes two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects
checks.explanation: Kindred I had renal salt wasting with autosomal dominant transmission. This is the renal-defect entity.

checks.claim: In the autosomal dominant PHA I kindred reported by Hanukoglu (1991), the disorder presented in infancy with renal salt wasting.
checks.evidence_quote: In kindred I, the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy

checks.claim: In the autosomal dominant PHA I kindred reported by Hanukoglu (1991), the disorder presented in infancy with hyperkalemia.
checks.evidence_quote: the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy (vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia)
checks.explanation: Hyperkalemia is listed among the infantile presenting features.

checks.claim: Hyperaldosteronism was documented in the autosomal dominant PHA I kindred reported by Hanukoglu (1991).
checks.evidence_quote: In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr

checks.claim: In the autosomal dominant PHA I kindred reported by Hanukoglu (1991), plasma renin activity was initially raised but fell gradually to near-normal values.
checks.evidence_quote: hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr; however, the PRA decreased gradually to near normal values
checks.explanation: A gradual fall to near-normal values implies PRA was raised at first.

checks.claim: Geller et al. (1998) described autosomal dominant PHA1 as a milder disease than the recessive form.
checks.evidence_quote: An autosomal recessive form features severe disease with manifestations persisting into adulthood. This form is caused by loss-of-function mutations in genes encoding subunits of the amiloride-sensitive epithelial sodium channel (ENaC; refs 2,3). Autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a milder disease that remits with age.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the dominant form milder and sets it against the severe recessive form.

checks.claim: Geller et al. (1998) described autosomal dominant PHA1 as remitting with age.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a milder disease that remits with age.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) distinguished 2 clinically and genetically distinct forms of PHA I. One is a renal form, limited to the kidney, in a kindred whose pedigree was consistent with autosomal dominant transmission. In the proband of this kindred, sodium supplementation was stopped at age 2 years. The other is a more severe form, in a kindred whose pedigree was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. In that form, multiple target organs do not respond to mineralocorticoids, as shown by increased salivary and sweat electrolytes.

checks.evidence_quote: type I PHA includes two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects

checks.claim: One form of PHA I distinguished by Hanukoglu (1991) is a renal form limited to the kidney.
checks.evidence_quote: type I PHA includes two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects
checks.explanation: One of the two entities is the renal form.

checks.claim: In the kindred with the renal form of PHA I reported by Hanukoglu (1991), the pedigree was consistent with autosomal dominant transmission.
checks.evidence_quote: The pedigree was consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission with variable expression.
checks.explanation: Stated for kindred I, which had the renal form.

checks.claim: The other form of PHA I distinguished by Hanukoglu (1991) is more severe and occurred in a kindred whose pedigree was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Life threatening episodes of salt wasting recurred beyond the age of 2 yr. At 5 yr of age she still requires high amounts of salt supplements (14 g/day).
checks.explanation: Kindred II was more severe, and its pedigree 'was consistent with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance'.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) studied 2 kindreds with a total of 9 patients with PHA. One kindred had the renal form. The proband presented in infancy with renal salt wasting, failure to thrive and hyperkalemia. He responded dramatically to a high-salt diet (2.5 g/day), and sodium supplementation was stopped at age 2 years. In other family members, clinical expression varied from asymptomatic to moderate. In the affected members (the proband, his mother and 2 brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted for 13 years, while plasma renin activity fell gradually to near-normal values. The pedigree was consistent with autosomal dominant transmission with variable expression. The dominant kindred ranged from asymptomatic to moderately affected, whereas the recessive case was severe.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) found that the renal form of PHA I was transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait with variable expression. Clinical expression ranged from asymptomatic to moderate, and hyperaldosteronism persisted in affected members. Tajima et al. (2000) noted that sporadic cases also occur.

checks.claim: Hanukoglu (1991) found that the renal form of PHA I was transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait with variable expression.
checks.evidence_quote: The pedigree was consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission with variable expression.

checks.claim: In the renal PHA I kindred reported by Hanukoglu (1991), clinical expression ranged from asymptomatic to moderate.
checks.evidence_quote: clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate

checks.claim: In the renal PHA I kindred reported by Hanukoglu (1991), hyperaldosteronism persisted in affected members.
checks.evidence_quote: In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr

checks.claim: Tajima et al. (2000) noted that sporadic cases of renal PHA I also occur.
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, in one sporadic and four dominant cases, four different mutations including two frame shift mutations, two premature termination codons, and one splice site mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) gene were identified.
checks.explanation: The paper notes a sporadic case alongside the dominant cases.

paragraphs.text: Geller et al. (1998) identified heterozygous mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (NR3C2) in kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA I. The mutations included frameshift, premature termination and splice donor mutations, and they segregated with PHA1.

checks.claim: Geller et al. (1998) identified heterozygous mutations in the NR3C2 gene in kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA I.
checks.evidence_quote: have identified heterozygous mutations in one sporadic and four dominant kindreds.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous MLR mutations were found in four dominant kindreds.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 mutations identified by Geller et al. (1998) in autosomal dominant PHA I included frameshift mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two frameshift mutations (one a de novo mutation), two premature termination codons and one splice donor mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists two frameshift mutations.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 mutations identified by Geller et al. (1998) in autosomal dominant PHA I included premature termination mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two frameshift mutations (one a de novo mutation), two premature termination codons and one splice donor mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists two premature termination codons.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 mutations identified by Geller et al. (1998) in autosomal dominant PHA I included splice donor mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two frameshift mutations (one a de novo mutation), two premature termination codons and one splice donor mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists one splice donor mutation. The draft's plural wording is a minor imprecision.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 mutations identified by Geller et al. (1998) segregated with PHA1 in the kindreds.
checks.evidence_quote: These mutations segregate with PHA1 and are not found in unaffected subjects.

paragraphs.text: In a family with renal PHA I, Tajima et al. (2000) identified a heterozygous missense mutation in the NR3C2 gene in all affected members. To their knowledge, it was the first missense mutation of NR3C2 reported in renal PHA1.

checks.claim: In a family with renal PHA I, Tajima et al. (2000) identified a heterozygous missense mutation in the NR3C2 gene in all affected members.
checks.evidence_quote: PCR and direct sequencing of the MR gene identified a heterozygous point mutation changing codon 924 Leu (CTG) to CCG (Pro) (L924P) in all affected members.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a heterozygous missense mutation (L924P) in all affected members of a family with renal PHA1.

checks.claim: To the knowledge of Tajima et al. (2000), the NR3C2 missense mutation they identified was the first missense mutation of NR3C2 reported in renal PHA1.
checks.evidence_quote: To our knowledge, this is the first case of the missense mutation of the MR gene in renal PHA1.

paragraphs.text: In a sporadic patient with renal PHA I, Viemann et al. (2001) identified a frameshift mutation in the NR3C2 gene. Family members were asymptomatic and did not carry the mutation, which indicated de novo occurrence. In 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1, Viemann et al. (2001) found no NR3C2 mutation.

checks.claim: In a sporadic patient with renal PHA I, Viemann et al. (2001) identified a frameshift mutation in the NR3C2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: In the sporadic case we identified a new frameshift mutation, Ins2871C, in exon 9 of the hMR gene.
checks.explanation: hMR is NR3C2. The case belongs to the 'autosomal dominant or sporadic form' (the renal form), though the abstract does not use the word 'renal'.

checks.claim: Family members of the sporadic renal PHA I patient reported by Viemann et al. (2001) were asymptomatic.
checks.evidence_quote: Family members were asymptomatic and had no mutation.

checks.claim: Family members of the sporadic renal PHA I patient reported by Viemann et al. (2001) did not carry the NR3C2 frameshift mutation, indicating de novo occurrence.
checks.evidence_quote: Family members were asymptomatic and had no mutation.
checks.explanation: Family members lacked the mutation. 'De novo' is not stated but follows directly from this.

checks.claim: In 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1, Viemann et al. (2001) found no NR3C2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: In 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1 we found no mutation of the hMR gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly. hMR is NR3C2.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) treated the proband of a dominant kindred in infancy with salt supplementation (a high-salt diet). Sodium supplementation was stopped at age 2 years.

checks.evidence_quote: the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy (vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia) and responded dramatically to a high salt diet (2.5 g/day)
